en: You handed over <Color:8>Mystery Item<Color:Default>.
(Okay, that's done. I can talk to the old-timer now.)
You got <Color:8>Mystery Item<Color:Default>.
Oh. Not good?
Basically, no one claimed they saw Baba do it, but nobody said he didn't, either.
Oh. Hm.
But doesn't it mean the guards can't prove he's the perp?
Well, I wouldn't count on that.
No?
The victim himself said Baba stabbed him. So that's direct evidence right there.
Direct evidence?
Yes, that's directly observing a crime happening. See, it's different from circumstantial evidence, which is observing something that logically indicates a crime is happening, or did.
Thanks for the mystery novel advice, but can we talk about what's important? Like whether the victim's account is enough to prove Baba's guilt?
By itself, it's not enough. But paired with the fact that Baba-chan was holding the bloody chisel...
See, that's a piece of circumstantial evidence, and a damn strong one. It perfectly backs up the direct evidence of the eyewitness testimony.
Himura, where'd you learn all this?
Baba said he didn't do it. Doncha believe 'im?
Yeah, we gotta believe Baba. The victim and his bunch are lying!
Naturally, that's a possibility.
But, there's nothing to back up that assertion.
(Damn...)
So, that's it? There's nothing we can do?
Well, there is one way...
Rather than trying to prove Baba-chan didn't do it...
We look for evidence that the woodworking crew is lying.
How do we do that?
With the chisel.
It had to be provided by either the victim himself or his pals.
Because, I mean, it's a woodworking tool. Where would Baba-chan even get it? He's not in the woodworking crew.
Baba could've taken the weapon from them.
Sure. But that theory is pretty shaky.
Because at the scene, the victim claimed Baba-chan just stabbed him out of the blue.
"Out of the blue" is not a phrase you would use if the weapon was taken from you or your friends.
It's a phrase that implies the weapon was already in Baba-chan's possession.
So, we still gotta find out where the chisel came from, then prove there was no way Baba coulda got his hands on it.
Yes! If we can prove that, it'll refute the victim's statement.
And of course, strengthen the argument that Baba-chan wasn't the perp.
Himura?
Why do you know so much about evidence and all?
Uh... Well, I'd appreciate it if you could keep this on the down low...
But you see, I was, uh... I used to be a detective with the Hokkaido Prefectural Police. Homicide, even.
What's a detective doin' behind bars?
Well, given the job, there's always... temptation.
I just... you know... got swept up in just a little teeny bit of corruption, is all.
And you didn't tell us.
Oshima, my job was finding and arresting criminals.
What do you think these inmates would do to me if they knew I used to be their enemy?
Yeah, good point.
It was just bribery. Heh. To be honest, my term's so short I thought there was a good chance I'd get out of here without anyone ever finding out about my background.
But now I've got a cellmate in deep trouble... a kid I break bread with every day. I can't just stand by and watch him go down.
I get it. And... hey, I think I've got some respect for you, even if you are a cop.
The quickest way out of this mess is finding out where the chisel came from.
Okay. So we ask around about that.
Right. Let's split up and do some legwork.
Hah. Spoken like a true detective.
I'm getting pumped! Let's do this!
This is bad!
Baba-chan wouldn't do something like that!
Of course not! He just submitted his request for parole.
No one in his position would do anything that might extend his sentence.
So true...
Saejima, what do you make of this?
(Prison's a rough place, is what I make of it.)
There's too much that we don't know.
Why don't we ask around to see if anyone can fill us in?
(Treatment took longer than I thought.)
(Baba-chan wasn't in the cell block. Is he out in the exercise yard?)
Heheh...
Those guys are in the woodworking crew.
You know what we want. The crew chief wants to see you.
Who are these guys, Saejima-aniki?
Stay out of this.
You got some kid you're trying to hide? Oh, if it isn't your little cellmate!
I get it. You're recruiting soldiers⑬nice, young ones you can turn into obedient little drones.
Not another word about the kid. I'm the one you want.
Fine, then. Come on.
(Huh, so Baba-chan's a killer. He seemed like such a friendly kid. Who woulda thought?)
(Where'd I see Baba-chan? On a bench up ahead, maybe.)
(Guess they don't cancel rec time no matter how cold it is.)
(Let's see... Anyone I know around?)
Your meal.
Something stopping you?
Deputy Warden... Why're ya here?
Answer my question. What's stopping you?
Nothin'. Just can't force nothin' down right now.
I don't mean the food. I mean Kugihara.
I know his men have been assaulting you. Why have you kept silent about it?
Do you think that being a model prisoner will get you out on parole sooner?
Don't count on it. In my penitentiary, no one who brings disorder is a model prisoner, even if he brings it unwillingly.
...That's especially true for those who plan to return to the underworld upon their release.
(...How does he know that?)
However, I'm also a prison officer. I can't turn a blind eye to physical attacks on an inmate under my care.
I can take steps to ensure you're kept away from Kugihara's gang.
(Ya think you're some guardian angel, eh?)
If you request it, I can keep you in solitary for the duration of your term.
All it would take is for me to inform the warden that you show no sign of remorse.
If I stay in solitary, the gang might go after the other guys in my cell.
So, you think they're your friends just because you share a cell.
Nah, nothin' like that. But I know if it ain't me, it'll be them gettin' beat. And they can't take it like I can. They'll end up leavin' prison feet-first.
Me, I can take being Kugihara's toy.
So you think you're saving others by serving yourself up? You think you're some guardian angel?
(...Me and this guy might be more alike than I wanna admit.)
I hate to break it to ya, but their only target is you.
Kugihara likes to cause trouble, but he's not stupid enough to assault just any random inmate.
So you're not accomplishing anything by putting up with such treatment.
Are ya done?
When you're finished eating, I'll let you out.
That's the only thing you want from me, isn't it?
What'd I tell you? Wasn't that a good way to lift your spirits?
Hah. All your stories have the stench of fresh, steaming bullshit.
Hey, all of it's true! Honest!
And besides, if you're going to fantasize you might as well make it a story with some sparkle, am I right?
After all, it'll be years before we can wine, dine, and be merry outside this place.
(I agree, Oshima.)
They can't keep us from enjoying life. Not when we know we'll get out of here someday.
That's why I'm okay with being here, paying my debt to society. We can put up with it as long as we keep dreaming about a tomorrow outside these walls.
All the fun in the world is waiting for us out there. We need to make amends so that we deserve it.
Don't you think that's a healthier way for us to think?
(It's somethin'.)
You're right. Being here does not define us.
We all had lives before, and we'll have them after. In the end, we'll die on the outside, on our own terms.
We should all be thinking about what we want to do when we're out.
Um, Saejima-san, I...
Welcome back! I didn't expect such a quick return from solitary.
Yeah. Not sure why, but the deputy warden just let me out.
Wait, you can't possibly mean⑬Kosaka!?
That doesn't sound right. He always comes down hard on inmates.
Well, I don't know the man's mind. All I know is he don't like yakuza. Made it clear I wasn't gettin' parole.
Now that sounds more like him.
He probably knows you're a big shot, and he's trying to discourage you from using prison as just another place to expand your network.
Even though Saejima foolishly wants to be in solitary. Hahaha! It's a crazy world. Don't you think, Baba-chan?
What's wrong? Hope you're not changing your mind.
You're still gonna apply for a new hearing tomorrow, right?
Your parole cancellation probably isn't official yet. There's still time.
If you go and demonstrate remorse, they might still let you out.
Hey, why we gotta put up with all the whimpering and shit!? Come on man, Saejima-san's back!
Why get all down in the dumps just 'cause Baba-chan wants to mope around? Let's talk about something enjoyable.
I know something!
A map?
This is a map of Sapporo's Tsukimino area.
It sure is. Everyone look at it and switch your minds over to the day when you can walk out of here and go anywhere in Tsukimino you want.
Switch our minds over?
Yeah. It's called image training.
You use your imagination, so that in your mind you're off having a good time in Tsukimino.
What good is that? It's like a children's game. Actually, it's stupider.
Lighten up, Pops. Come on, it'll be a welcome change from these dreary surroundings. Right, Saejima-san? You'll do it, huh?
Come on, Baba! You need it the most!
Good. Everyone ready? I want you to picture the streets of Tsukimino in your mind.
Don't know Tsukimino that well, actually. Can't picture it.
Huh? Right, you're not from the north. Well then, how about we try this? Listen.
I'll tell you a story from when I was there. Saejima-san, you just imagine the situations I describe as if you were me.
At the end you'll feel like it all really happened to you.
Hm. All right...
Okay, here we go.
We not goin' to solitary?
Why didn't you stop?
That fight. Why didn't you stop?
Funny thing. Short while ago, ya asked why I <Italic>wasn't</Italic> fightin'. Remember?
Your parole application. I spent the last few days writing it.
Why? Ya said ya don't let yakuza out.
A week ago, the warden received this postcard here.
It's a formal notice expelling you from the Tojo Clan.
This penitentiary's purpose is to reform those who have committed crimes.
Inmates who demonstrate sufficient reformation can expect reductions in their sentences.
Parole is one such reduction.
If an inmate is associated with yakuza, his most effective means of proving he is reformed is to renounce all associations with organized crime.
And... it appears this applies to your case.
I know you were going to be named captain when you got out.
Two years ago, when you arrived here, the police included a note in your file.
They recommended that your future promotion be kept secret from the other inmates.
Three years... just for assault. There are only two reasons why someone would serve that kind of time for such a minor charge.
One: you were set up by a hostile third party, specifically so you'd be forced to leave your organization.
Or two: you chose to tidy up your affairs... for the sake of that very organization.
All these beatings in prison, and you didn't defend yourself because you just wanted to return to the clan as soon as you could. Am I correct?
I'm expelled. It's pointless now.
I'm going to overlook what happened today.
The relevant factor is that you are no longer yakuza. There's no need for you to continue suffering here.
What? You're crying?
Hey! Quiet!
Well... I guess it is leisure time... but don't be loud! Or I'll hand out demerits.
Sorry, sir!
Saejima. Baba.
Both of you come with me. We need to go over the work you did the other day.
Uh, yes sir.
Come on, Saejima. Get up.
Aniki.
Himura-san!
Hey, I was a homicide detective, remember?
My tales of glory aren't full of as much bullshit as you all seem to think!
By the way, Oshima-san is dealing with the deputy warden. It might be dicey, but at least you shouldn't get any trouble from him while you make your getaway.
Dead serious. Haha, Oshima, that rascally old geezer... You know how he'd hoard meds and pass them to other inmates?
Turns out that's a habit left over from his brief time as a doctor. Who the heck moves on from being a doctor, then ends up in prison?
Boy, you never can know someone, eh?
Whatever past any of you have, I'm just relieved we're getting out!
That's right. You guys need to go. I'll call the authorities and play dumb when they arrive.
Don't get caught if you can help it!
What about you and Oshima-san?
You know us⑬we're gonna be good boys and serve out our prison sentences.
